legend: Bronchial cell hyperplasia with crowded tissue fragment of oriented columnar cells with nuclear multilayering and cilia (bronchial washing, H&E).
Multinucleated bronchial cells with typical nuclei showing irregular rim of chromatin and central blurred inclusion of herpes simplex virus (tracheal washing, Pap).
Small flat sheet of bland basal cells in the upper half of the photo; in the lower half, normal ciliated bronchial epithelium (bronchial brushing, H&E).
Small flat sheet of bland basal cells at the right; at the left, normal ciliated epithelium (bronchial brushing, Giemsa); same case as in Fig. <<24916>>.
Small flat sheet of reactive bronchial epithelium with large nuclei, macronucleoli, a bland chromatin pattern, and well-demarcated cytoplasm (bronchial brushing, H&E).

Small flat sheet of reactive bronchial epithelium with large nuclei and regular nuclear membrane, some macronucleoli, a bland chromatin pattern, and one mitotic figure (bronchial washing, Giemsa); same case as in Fig. <<24919>>.

Loosely cohesive tissue fragment of large bronchial epithelial cells with mild anisonucleosis, enlarged nuclei, regular nuclear membranes, prominent macronucleoli, and a fine chromatin pattern. The cells are pulled out with long cytoplasmic interconnections between the cells. Some cells are binucleated (bronchial washing, Pap).
Metaplastic squamous cells of medium size, with round to oval mildly pleomorphic nuclei that have bland chromatin, and with dense, opaque cytoplasm (bronchial washing, H&E).

Metaplastic squamous cells of medium size, with low N:C ratio, round to oval hyperchromatic nuclei, and dense and opaque but not keratinized cytoplasm. At the upper left are two large squamous cells of the upper respiratory tract (bronchial washing, Pap); same case as in Fig. <<24922>>.
Detached ciliary tuft with some attached cytoplasm of a bronchial cell with neutrophils in a bronchial washing (bronchial washing, Pap).
Binucleated pneumocyte with characteristic large eosinophilic nuclear inclusion with surrounding clearing (bronchoalveolar lavage [BAL], H&E).
Pneumocyte with positive CMV nuclear ICC staining (bronchial washing).

In the centre are two infected cells, each with a large, opaque viral inclusion surrounded by clearing (the characteristic owl-eye appearance), in a background of plentiful macrophages (bronchoalveolar lavage [BAL], Pap).

legend: Imaging showed pulmonary infiltrates during chemotherapy for malignant lymphoma (R-CHOP 14). Bronchial epithelium with reactive changes including enlarged nuclei with smudged chromatin, fine cytoplasmic vacuoles, and loss of cilia (bronchial washing, H&E).

Pulmonary infiltrates during chemotherapy for malignant lymphoma (R-CHOP 14). Bronchial epithelium with reactive changes including large, crowded tissue fragments of cells with enlarged nuclei, some macronucleoli, and focal loss of cilia (bronchial washing, Pap).

Pulmonary infiltrates during chemotherapy for malignant lymphoma (R-CHOP 14). Bronchial epithelium with severe reactive changes, including cytomegaly, some cells with enlarged hyperchromatic nuclei that have blurred chromatin, large cytoplasmic vacuoles, and focal loss of cilia (bronchial washing, Pap).

Pulmonary mass lesion and history of high-dose chemotherapy, autologous and allogenous stem cell transplantation for malignant lymphoma 5 years previously. Squamous metaplasia with nuclear atypia in a background of ciliated bronchial cells and numerous neutrophils (bronchial brushing, H&E).

Pulmonary mass lesion and history of high-dose chemotherapy, autologous and allogenous stem cell transplantation for malignant lymphoma 5 years previously. Squamous metaplasia with nuclear atypia, low N:C ratio, and abundant dense eosinophilic cytoplasm in a background of ciliated bronchial cells and numerous neutrophils (bronchial brushing, H&E).

Pulmonary mass lesion and history of high-dose chemotherapy, autologous and allogenous stem cell transplantation for malignant lymphoma 5 years previously. Several cells show squamous metaplasia with nuclear atypia and denser concentric cytoplasm, in a background of ciliated bronchial cells neutrophils (bronchial brushing, Giemsa).

Imaging showed pulmonary infiltrates after high-dose chemotherapy for acute myeloid leukaemia. Bronchial epithelium with reactive changes including enlarged nuclei with smudged chromatin, dense cytoplasm, and loss of cilia (sputum sample, Pap).
